doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

chapter: Johnny Hammond, Dreams and moving to New York
title: Choice versus necessity, Billy Cobham and Jack DeJohnette's call
summary: He took many gigs out of need, worked with Cobham, then DeJohnette phoned him, pulling him back from pure fusion.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You seem to have had your tastes in a lot of different places. Has it always been of your own choosing?

No. I mean I think it gets mixed up. Sometimes it’s hard to know whether or not it’s your own choosing. Sometimes you find yourself in a situation that you think you wanted to get in and then once you’re in it you realize you shouldn’t be there. I’d say since I started playing this music, most of it’s been pretty much stuff I like to do. It hasn’t always been my own choosing. Sometimes somebody will hire me and I need the gig. Especially when I was younger and I would take any gig that was offered to me from the time I started working in Boston and as a musician until I moved to New York, where do I go, how much do I make, what do I have to play. And then as I got a little older and I sort of found myself getting a little bit of a reputation I found that I could do more of what I wanted to do, not that I could do everything I wanted to do for sure, I still can’t, but more or less, especially once I started recording for ECM and starting to develop more of an identity, you know, and I had my own records. And that happened pretty quickly in the early 70s, around ’74. And before that I had worked with Billy Cobham, which was a great experience. And that was like a return to the Dreams band because it also had

Michael and Randy. And then I got a phone call one morning from Jack DeJohnette and he just asked me if I wanted to come up and play at his house. And I said sure. So I went up and we played and we started a relationship, and that would sort of pull me back away from the pure fusion music and put me back closer to where I had started.
